title: The Canticle, read whole
hookLine: brother sun, sister moon, brother wind, sister water, brother fire, mother earth
tomorrow: what do you do with the people you never got to pick?

lines: ROOM FOR A LINE OR TWO.
cards: Brother Sun. Sister Moon. Brother Wind.
Sister Water. Brother Fire. Sister, Mother Earth.
Read the names aloud and it sounds like a family reunion where everyone gets a nickname, even the weather. A line or two of Francis of Assisi's song turns up on garden plaques and greeting cards.
A plaque only has room for a line or two. The whole Canticle keeps going, past the garden, to a place a greeting card wouldn't follow. So, the whole thing, start to finish.

teach.b: It opens with God alone: most high, all-powerful, good Lord, yours are the praise, the glory and the honor. Then the refrain: praised be you, my Lord, with all your creatures.
Brother Sun, who brings the day, beautiful and radiant, bearing your likeness. Sister Moon and the stars, clear and precious and fair. Brother Wind, and air and cloud and every kind of weather.
Sister Water, useful and humble and precious and pure. Brother Fire, cheerful and strong. Sister, our Mother Earth, who sustains us, with fruits and colored flowers.
Then the song turns to people: praised be you for those who forgive for love of you, and bear sickness and trouble.
And then: praised be you, my Lord, for our Sister Bodily Death, whom no one living can escape. Francis gives even death a family name.
One small word in his dialect, per, can mean for, or by, or through, so the refrain can be heard more than one way: praised for the sun, by the sun, through the sun. The song doesn't settle it.
The last line calls everything home: praise and bless my Lord, give thanks, and serve him with great humility.
And listen to how it gathers the week: a present moment worth praising, beginners, the sick, people who forgive. The Canticle is a family where nobody is left off the list, not even the hard members.

how: Franciscans and other Christians sing or pray the Canticle of the Creatures, sometimes outdoors, and it appears in hymn versions sung in churches.

games.q: a friend wants the Canticle on a graduation card, but only the sun-and-moon lines. what gets left out?
o: nothing much; the rest is repetition.
the people who forgive, and Sister Death.

games.why: read whole, the song turns from creatures to people who forgive and bear trouble, and then praises God even for Sister Bodily Death.

practice: If you can, step outside or stand at a window, and walk a few slow steps or just turn your head. Name what's actually there in Francis's way, one at a time: brother sun, sister rain, brother wind.
If you pray, add his refrain to each: praised be you, my Lord.

wordCard.voice: The Canticle. Francis of Assisi's song praising God with sun, moon, wind, water, fire and earth, and on through forgiveness and death.

orig.note: the refrain in Francis's own Italian dialect, close to Latin: praised be you, my Lord.

carryVoice: Your line: praised be, my Lord. The song starts with the sun and doesn't skip the hard members of the family. That's the week.
